name: security-gcp-workload-identity-pool-review
intent: Workload Identity Federation provider claims and service-account delegation
artifacts: Pool/provider issuer, attribute mappings/conditions, principal bindings and impersonation chain.
trace: Trace external issuer claims into effective principals and distinguish provider admission from permission to impersonate a service account.
experiment: Use an owned local claim-policy fixture or isolated test provider with two synthetic workloads; compare intended subject and a controlled claim mismatch.
disproof: Token exchange success alone does not establish target resource access; the impersonation/resource policy may still deny.
repair: Bind issuer attributes and delegation to the intended workload, then verify approved jobs and unrelated workload denial.
branch_decisions: Evaluate issuer, audience, attribute mapping and provider conditions before IAM principal/principalSet bindings. Attribute values such as repository name can be reassigned; immutable producer IDs may have different trust properties. Direct resource access and service-account impersonation are separate grants; a successful token exchange alone establishes neither final permission.
